newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound slides as sterling soars to 59-mth hig.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound slides as sterling soars to 59-mth hig.

text.p: The Irish pound lost nearly half a penny against sterling in morning trade on Friday as the UK unit powered to a new 59-month high of 2.8880 marks.

Dealers said sterling's surge was driven by buoyant first quarter growth figures, an upward revision to fourth quarter British GDP and growing concern over EMU after France admitted that it will not cut its deficit this year to three percent of GDP.
Analysts say that if sterling's run continues, it could put further downward pressure on the Irish pound, fuelling fears of inflation.

"Sterling has very clearly targeted 2.90 marks in its head. We may well see that before the budget and it could pose real problems for the Irish pound," said Colin Hunt, economist at Bank of Ireland Group Treasury.

By 1138 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9040 sterling, down from an earlier high of 0.9085 and 0.9073 at Thursday's close. It hovered broadly unchanged around 2.6100 marks, standing at 2.6109 marks against 2.6122 yesterday.
Dealers said 0.9000 sterling would prove a key psychological level and if the Irish pound were to break below this, it would set alarm bells ringing on the inflation front.
"If you were to see a sustained break below 0.9000, you would hear some voices at the central bank calling for a rate rise," one trader said.
All eyes will now be on UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's budget next week to see its impact on sterling, dealers said.
